Table-aware ingestion decreased retrieval performance because near-duplicate chunks crowded the re-ranker and displaced answer-bearing narrative chunks.

Most RAG projects skip the golden-question evaluation harness that proves retrieval quality with numbers rather than vibes. When testing CiteRAG on Berkshire Hathaway annual reports, the initial naive retrieval pipeline achieved a recall@5 of 0.367. Adding a re-ranker improved this to 0.500, but increasing the re-rank pool from 20 to 50 candidates was rejected because it decreased recall@5 from 0.733 to 0.700.

Evaluation sets matter. A 30-question set incorrectly suggested that re-ranker quality was the binding constraint, whereas a 60-question set identified query rewriting as the primary need. Even small technical details like re-spacing welded text: +0.033 with the re-ranker, +0.067 without it can shift results. Measuring the mechanism itself is more reliable than trusting proxies.

bodies.thread:
Table-aware ingestion actually hurt retrieval performance. It decreased recall@5 from 0.733 to 0.667 because near-duplicate chunks crowded the re-ranker and displaced answer-bearing narrative chunks.

The system uses SQLite and sqlite-vec for a zero-infrastructure, local implementation. It avoids LLM dependencies for both retrieval and the evaluation harness.

Embedding models often blur dense financial data like dollar amounts or tickers. A keyword index is needed to nail those exact tokens.

The project uses Berkshire Hathaway annual reports from 2021 to 2023. This corpus contains dense, complex financial data that serves as a difficult retrieval target.

A bug in the segmentation logic caused the system to skip all-lowercase welds at sentence starts. Fixing this reduced welds to 3.7% of tokens.

Doubling the evaluation set from 30 to 60 questions changed the project's priorities. The smaller set incorrectly pointed to re-ranker quality, while the larger set identified query rewriting as the primary need.

Relying on qualitative impressions is a mistake. A system must include a golden-question evaluation harness to objectively prove retrieval quality.
